home.description: RawMask Studio is an iPhone photo editor for RAW photos with automatic and manual masks. Everything runs on your iPhone.
home.help: Questions or problems? Visit the support page. Details about how the app handles your photos are in the privacy policy.

support.title: Support - RawMask Studio
support.description: Help and contact for RawMask Studio for iPhone: opening photos, Photos access, masks, saving, and exporting.
support.meta: Help for RawMask Studio for iPhone.
support.ui_labels_note: Button and menu names below are in English, exactly as they appear in the app.
support.contact_note: Please include your iPhone model, iOS version, and a short description of what happened and what you expected. There is no need to send photos; describing the photo (for example, the camera or file format) is usually enough.

faq.q: How do I open a photo?

blocks.p: Tap the photo button at the top left of the editor and choose Open photo. The Photos picker opens, and you choose one photo. RawMask Studio edits one photo at a time. Live Photos are not currently shown in the picker.
RAW photos that Apple's built-in RAW support can read, including Apple ProRAW and RAW files from many cameras, as well as regular photos such as HEIC and JPEG.

faq.q: Why does the app ask for Photos access?

blocks.p: RawMask Studio opens photos from, and saves edits back to, your Apple Photos library, so iOS asks for your permission. You can allow full access or limited access to only the photos you pick. Either way, the app only opens the photo you choose. See the privacy policy for details.

faq.q: I chose limited access and cannot find a photo

blocks.p: With limited access, the app can only open the photos you have allowed. To allow more photos:

ul: In the app, tap More options (the ... button), then under Photos access tap Manage allowed photos, or
open Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > RawMask Studio and change the selection or choose Full Access.

faq.q: The app says Photos access is off

blocks.p: Open Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > RawMask Studio, choose Limited Access or Full Access, then return to the app and open a photo again.

Adjustments apply either to the whole photo or to a mask. Open the photo button menu at the top left: use Edit target to choose what you are editing, and Add mask to add a Radial, Linear, Brush, or Rectangle mask. You can move and resize a mask, paint to add to or subtract from it, and soften its edge with Feather.

RawMask Studio includes an image segmentation model that finds objects in your photo, such as people, animals, and everyday things, and offers each one as a mask you can edit on its own. The model runs entirely on your iPhone. If it does not pick up the object you want, use a manual mask instead, or adjust Detection confidence and Mask threshold under More options > Advanced > Object detection.

faq.q: Do I need an internet connection?

blocks.p: No. Editing and automatic masks work offline. The one exception is a photo stored in iCloud Photos whose original is not on your iPhone: Photos has to download the original from iCloud before it can be edited.

faq.q: How do I save or export my edit?

blocks.p: Tap More options (the ... button) and go to Save and export:

ul: Save edit to Photos updates the photo in your library. Photos keeps the original, so you can go back to it later with Revert in the Photos app.
Save a copy to Photos adds the edited image as a new photo and leaves the original unchanged.
Export photo creates a JPEG, HEIF, or TIFF file in the size and quality you choose and opens the share sheet, so you can save it to Files or send it to another app.

blocks.p: On your iPhone, in the app's own storage. They are not uploaded anywhere. You can delete presets in the app, and deleting the app removes them.
iPhone with iOS 17 or later.

faq.q: Does RawMask Studio collect my data?

blocks.p: No. There is no account, analytics, advertising, or tracking, and the app does not send your photos or data to us or to anyone else. Read the full privacy policy.

support.still_text: Email turmanauli.beso@gmail.com and we will get back to you.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy - RawMask Studio
privacy.description: Privacy policy for RawMask Studio for iPhone. The app does not collect any data; photos are edited on your iPhone.
privacy.meta: RawMask Studio for iPhone. Effective date: September 23, 2026.
privacy.summary: In short: RawMask Studio does not collect any data. There is no account, no analytics, no advertising, and no tracking. Your photos are edited on your iPhone, and the app never sends your photos, your edits, or any other information to us or to anyone else.

blocks.p: RawMask Studio is developed and published by Besarion Turmanauli, an individual developer. In this policy, "we", "us", and "our" refer to the developer. You can reach us using the details in Contact below.

None. RawMask Studio does not collect, transmit, sell, or share personal information. The app does not send your photos, edits, masks, presets, settings, device identifiers, usage data, or diagnostics to us or to any third party, and we do not operate any server that receives data from the app. There is no sign-in and no account.
All photo processing happens on your device. This includes reading RAW files, applying light, color, detail, focus, and effects adjustments, rendering previews, and creating masks.

Automatic object masks are created by an image segmentation model (RF-DETR) that is included inside the app and runs on your iPhone using Apple's Core ML. The model is not downloaded from the internet, and your photos are not sent anywhere to be analyzed.

RawMask Studio uses Apple Photos to open and save pictures. iOS asks for your permission before the app can access your library. You can allow access to your full library or only to the photos you select, and you can change this at any time in Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > RawMask Studio.

Only the photo you choose in the photo picker, one photo at a time. To edit it, the app reads that photo's image data and the details needed for editing, such as its dimensions, capture date, file format, and any earlier RawMask Studio edit saved with it. The app does not browse, scan, or index the rest of your library.
Nothing, unless you ask it to. Nothing is saved to your library automatically.

ul: Save edit to Photos saves the edited version to that photo in your library, together with a record of your edit settings that Photos keeps with the photo so the edit can be reopened later. Photos keeps the original, and you can revert to it in the Photos app.
Save a copy to Photos adds the edited image as a new photo. The original is not changed.

blocks.p: If you use iCloud Photos and the full-resolution original of the photo you choose is not stored on your iPhone, Apple's Photos framework may download it from iCloud so it can be edited. Photos you save may also be synced by iCloud Photos according to your Apple settings. These transfers take place between your device and your own iCloud account, are handled by Apple, and are covered by Apple's privacy policy. Nothing is sent to us.

When you tap Export photo, the app creates the image file you asked for and opens the iOS share sheet. The file goes only where you choose to send it, such as Files, Messages, or another app, and that destination handles it under its own privacy practices. The temporary file the app creates for the export is kept in the app's private storage on your iPhone and is deleted automatically when it is no longer needed.
So that the app works the way you left it, it keeps a small amount of information in its own storage on your iPhone:

ul: presets you save (their names and adjustment values),
editor preferences, such as which editing sections are shown, their order, and the before and after comparison style, and

blocks.p: This information stays on your device and is not sent to us. You can delete a preset in the app at any time, and deleting the app removes all of this information. Like other app data, it may be included in backups of your iPhone that you make, according to your iOS settings.

sections.h2: No third-party services, analytics, advertising, or tracking

blocks.p: RawMask Studio contains no third-party analytics, advertising, crash reporting, or tracking software. It does not use the advertising identifier and does not track you across apps or websites owned by other companies.

If you have chosen in iOS to share analytics with app developers (Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements), Apple may give us crash reports and aggregated usage statistics in a form that does not identify you. This is controlled by Apple and by your settings, not by the app.

RawMask Studio is currently free. If in-app purchases or paid features are added in the future, payments will be processed by Apple through the App Store under Apple's terms and privacy policy, and we will not receive your payment details. We will update this policy before any such change takes effect.

RawMask Studio is a general photo editing app and is not specifically directed to children. Because the app does not collect personal information from anyone, it does not collect personal information from children.

Because we do not collect or hold any data about you, there is no personal data on our side to access, correct, export, or delete. You stay in control on your device: you can change or revoke Photos access in iOS Settings, delete presets in the app, remove edits or copies in the Photos app, and delete the app to remove its local data.

If the way the app handles information changes, for example if a future feature needs to send data off your device, we will update this policy and the app's App Store privacy details before that version is released, and we will change the effective date at the top of this page.
If you have a question about this policy or about your privacy when using RawMask Studio, contact:
